questions.question: How many days of annual leave do full-time employees get per year?
questions.answer: According to the Leave Policy v2 (2. Annual leave): “Full-time employees accrue 16 days of annual leave per calendar year, credited each pay period in equal parts. Part-time employees accrue pro rata.” [1]
questions.expected: 16 days (Leave Policy v2, which supersedes v1's 12 days).
questions.judge_reason: The answer gives the current in-force v2 entitlement of 16 days per year, matching the reference.

questions.question: How much vacation do I get?
questions.answer: According to the Leave Policy v2 (2. Annual leave): “Full-time employees accrue 16 days of annual leave per calendar year, credited each pay period in equal parts. Part-time employees accrue pro rata.” [1]
questions.expected: 16 days of annual leave per calendar year.
questions.judge_reason: The answer gives the reference key fact of 16 days of annual leave per calendar year and adds supported details without contradiction.

questions.question: How many sick days do employees get a year?
questions.answer: According to the Leave Policy v2 (3. Sick leave): “Employees receive 8 days of sick leave per year. A doctor's note is required for absences of three or more consecutive days.” [1]
questions.expected: 8 days of sick leave per year.
questions.judge_reason: The answer gives the referenced entitlement of 8 sick leave days per year and the cited policy is in force on the question date.

questions.question: How many unused leave days can I carry into next year, and when do they expire?
questions.answer: According to the Leave Policy v2 (4. Carry forward): “Up to 8 unused annual leave days may be carried into the next calendar year. Carried days must be used by March 31 or they lapse.” [1]
questions.expected: Up to 8 days; they must be used by March 31.
questions.judge_reason: The answer matches the reference: up to 8 days may be carried forward and they expire if not used by March 31.

questions.question: Who needs to approve leave of more than ten consecutive working days?
questions.answer: According to the Leave Policy v2 (5. Approval): “Leave of more than ten consecutive working days also needs the department head's approval. Managers should respond to requests within two working days.” [1]
questions.expected: The direct manager and also the department head.
questions.judge_reason: It correctly states department head approval is needed but omits that the employee's direct manager must also approve the leave.

questions.question: How long before a scheduled release does the deploy freeze start?
questions.answer: According to the Production Deploy Runbook (1. When to deploy): “A deploy freeze starts 72 hours before every scheduled release and during declared incidents. Freeze exceptions need the on-call manager's approval in #deploys.” [1]
questions.expected: 72 hours (the deprecated 2023 runbook said 36 hours).
questions.judge_reason: The answer gives the in-force runbook value of 72 hours before a scheduled release, matching the reference.

questions.question: How long after a deploy can I use the one-click rollback?
questions.answer: According to the Production Deploy Runbook (4. Rollback window): “A deploy can be rolled back with a single click in the deploy console for 45 minutes after full rollout completes. After that window, rollback requires a new deploy of the previous version following the Rollback Procedure.” [1]
questions.expected: 45 minutes after full rollout completes (2023 runbook said 10 minutes).
questions.judge_reason: The answer gives the in-force 45-minute rollback window after full rollout completes and does not contradict the reference.

questions.question: How many approving reviews does a change to a production repository need?
questions.answer: According to the Code Review Guidelines: “Every change to a production repository needs 2 approving review(s) from someone other than the author before merge, plus a green CI pipeline. Reviews should be returned within one working day; if you cannot review in time, say so and suggest someone else.” [1]
questions.expected: 2 approving reviews from someone other than the author, plus green CI.
questions.judge_reason: The answer gives the required 2 approving reviews from non-authors plus green CI, matching the reference; the extra review-timing detail is supported.

questions.question: How long does the canary stage run and how much traffic does it get?
questions.answer:
According to the Production Deploy Runbook (3. Rollout): “Deploys go through the canary stage (5 percent of traffic) for ten minutes, then to full rollout. Watch the error rate and p95 latency dashboards during the canary.” [1]

Also relevant, from the Database Migration Runbook: “Take a snapshot immediately before running the migration and verify that the snapshot is restorable in staging first.” [2]
questions.expected: Ten minutes at 5 percent of traffic.
questions.judge_reason: The answer gives the key facts that the canary runs for ten minutes at 5 percent of traffic, with only extra supported information.

questions.question: How many weeks of paid leave do secondary caregivers get?
questions.answer:
According to the Parental Leave Policy (Secondary caregiver leave): “Fathers and secondary caregivers receive 12 weeks of fully paid leave, to be taken within six months of the birth or adoption.” [1]

Upcoming change: the Parental Leave Policy (2027 revision) takes effect on 2027-01-01 and says: “Following the 2026 benefits review, secondary caregiver leave increases from 12 weeks to 26 weeks fully paid for births and adoptions on or after 2027-01-01.” [2] Until then the rule above applies.
questions.expected: 12 weeks today; 26 weeks for births/adoptions on or after 2027-01-01.
questions.judge_reason: The answer gives the current 12-week entitlement and the upcoming 26-week entitlement for births/adoptions on or after 2027-01-01, matching the reference.

questions.question: My partner is due in March 2027. How much paid leave will I get as the secondary caregiver?
questions.answer:

Upcoming change: the Parental Leave Policy (2027 revision) takes effect on 2027-01-01 and says: “Following the 2026 benefits review, secondary caregiver leave increases from 12 weeks to 26 weeks fully paid for births and adoptions on or after 2027-01-01.” [2] Until then the rule above applies.
questions.expected: 26 weeks fully paid (2027 revision applies to births on or after 2027-01-01).
questions.judge_reason: The answer includes the applicable 26-week entitlement for a March 2027 birth, but it does not clearly state that this is the user's entitlement and foregrounds the current 12-week rule, making the key answer somewhat buried.

Upcoming change: the Parental Leave Policy (2027 revision) takes effect on 2027-01-01 and says: “Birth parent leave is unchanged at 16 weeks.” [2] Until then the rule above applies.
questions.expected: 16 weeks of fully paid leave.
questions.judge_reason: The answer gives the reference key fact that birth parents get 16 weeks of fully paid leave and only adds supported details.

questions.answer:
